claims.claim: The largest dam removal in U.S. history began on the Elwha River on September 17, 2011.
claims.episode_span: workers on Washington’s Elwha River began the largest dam-removal project in U.S. history
claims.source_title: Elwha River Restoration - Olympic National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
claims.supporting_quote: the largest dam removal in U.S. history began on September 17, 2011

claims.claim: Congress authorized removal of the Elwha River dams via the Elwha River Ecosystem and Fisheries Restoration Act of 1992.
claims.episode_span: Congress authorized removal of the two Elwha River dams in 1992
claims.source_title: Elwha River Restoration - Olympic National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
claims.supporting_quote: In 1992, Congress passed the Elwha River Ecosystem and Fisheries Restoration Act , authorizing dam removal to restore the altered ecosystem

claims.claim: The Elwha dams blocked fish from over 70 miles of habitat, and Chinook salmon appeared upstream within months of the Elwha Dam's removal.
claims.episode_span: Within months, Chinook salmon that had been barred from 70 miles of upstream habitat began appearing again
claims.source_title: Return of the Kings - Olympic National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
claims.supporting_quote: When the Elwha Dam became operational in 1913, twenty-five years before the establishment of the park, over 70 miles of habitat were blocked to fish passage

claims.claim: Elwha Dam removal began September 2011; both dams were gone by 2014 (Elwha Dam by March 2012, Glines Canyon Dam in 2014).
claims.episode_span: deconstruction began in 2011 and was largely complete by 2014
claims.source_title: Elwha River Restoration - Olympic National Park (U.S. National Park Service)
claims.supporting_quote: Six months later the Elwha Dam was gone, followed by the Glines Canyon Dam in 2014

claims.claim: Grand Coulee Dam's groundbreaking was in 1933, with funds for Bonneville Dam approved days later; Bonneville's first powerhouse was constructed 1933-37 and Grand Coulee was completed in 1942.
claims.episode_span: Construction began on Bonneville Dam in 1933 and on Grand Coulee in 1933; both were completed before the end of World War II
claims.source_title: Washington: Grand Coulee Dam (U.S. National Park Service)
claims.supporting_quote: Groundbreaking ceremonies took place on July 16, 1933, just days before funds were approved for another dam on the Columbia River--the huge Bonneville Dam

claims.claim: Grand Coulee Dam was completed in 1942 and powered WWII aluminum production.
claims.episode_span: both were completed before the end of World War II
claims.source_title: Washington: Grand Coulee Dam (U.S. National Park Service)
claims.supporting_quote: Grand Coulee took eight years to build, employed thousands of men during the Great Depression and, when completed in 1942, provided the enormous electrical power necessary to make aluminum

claims.claim: More than 40 percent of the salmon and steelhead habitat once available in the Columbia River Basin is permanently blocked by dams.
claims.episode_span: estimates suggest that roughly 40 percent of historic salmon and steelhead habitat was blocked by the mid-1960s
claims.source_title: Dams: impacts on salmon and steelhead - Northwest Power and Conservation Council
claims.supporting_quote: More than 40 percent of the spawning and rearing habitat once available to salmon and steelhead in the Columbia River Basin is permanently blocked by dams

claims.claim: Through the 1990s a succession of Columbia Basin salmon and steelhead populations were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
claims.episode_span: by the 1990s several Columbia River stocks were listed under the Endangered Species Act
claims.source_title: Endangered Species Act - Northwest Power and Conservation Council
claims.supporting_quote: Through the 1990s, one salmon or steelhead population after another was listed for protection under the ESA as run sizes continued to decline

claims.claim: A 2016 arrangement scheduled four Klamath River dams for removal; all four were removed by August 2024.
claims.episode_span: On the Klamath, a 2016 agreement led to the drawdown of the four lower dams beginning in 2023
claims.supporting_quote: In 2016, four of the project's dams were scheduled for removal by the year 2020, pending approval by the governing Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

claims.claim: The total cost of the Elwha River restoration was approximately $351.4 million, i.e. more than $300 million.
claims.episode_span: The financial cost of removal—more than $300 million for the Elwha project alone
claims.source_title: Restoration of the Elwha River - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The total cost of the Elwha River restoration is approximately $351.4 million
